FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.99  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.18  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment` has annotated fields and uses `field(...)`, but it is missing `@dataclass` and has no explicit `__init__`. `assign()` calls `cls(role_map=..., capability_scores=..., ...)`, so the class is not constructible as written and fails before any role logic runs.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `@dataclass` to `RoleAssignment` or implement an explicit `__init__` that initializes `role_map`, `capability_scores`, `pm_model_id`, `_config`, `_models`, and `_failure_history`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` documents `active_models=None` as “all models active”, but it actually uses `set(self.role_map.keys())`. Because `self.role_map` is overwritten with only the most recent active subset, inactive models drop out of the registry and recovered models cannot re-enter when the caller later uses the default.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Derive the default active set from the immutable model pool (`self._models`), not from `self.role_map`, and keep activeness separate from the total assignment registry.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` decides whether to create a `COL` using `len(self._models) >= 3`, which is the original pool size, not the current active size. If the run starts with 3+ models but only 2 remain active, it still assigns a `COL`, contradicting the area’s own “COL if K >= 3” rule.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Gate `COL` creation on the current active-model count, and define the fallback behavior explicitly for active `K < 3`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: The advertised deterministic tie-break is not fully implemented. `reassign()` uses `max(col_scores, key=...)` without `_tie_break_key`, and `remaining_ids` comes from a set, so equal-score `COL` choices can vary by hash iteration order. `assign()` and `get_ordering()` also fall back to input/dict order when score and fingerprint ties are exact.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use a single canonical ordering everywhere, e.g. `(score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)`, and avoid set-order-dependent winner selection.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` can score models using live fingerprints and failure-history penalties, but it never refreshes `self.capability_scores`. After the first reassignment, `get_ordering()` exposes stale initial rankings and may include models that are no longer active, so the public state no longer matches the actual decision rule.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute stored scores on reassignment, or split immutable baseline scores from current effective scores and expose both explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.31  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` never validates that `model_id` values are unique. Because all internal maps are keyed by `model_id`, duplicates silently overwrite one another in `scores`, `role_map`, and `_failure_history`, collapsing multiple models into one logical actor.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate uniqueness of all `model_id` values before scoring and raise a clear error on duplicates.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: Public APIs accept contradictory or unknown model IDs without validation. In `reassign()`, an unknown ID can be skipped during scoring and then still be inserted as `PAR`; omitting the locked PM from `active_models` is silently ignored because PM is always reinserted; `record_failure()` creates history for unknown IDs.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate every external model ID against the original pool, reject unknown IDs, and raise if `active_models` omits the locked PM instead of silently repairing caller input.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` accepts `round_idx` but never uses it, and failure history is append-based rather than round-indexed. That means `phi_hist(m, r-1)` is really “mean over however many times `record_failure()` happened to be called”, so duplicate/missing calls or inactive rounds distort the penalty silently.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store failure history keyed by round, enforce at most one record per model per round, and either use `round_idx` for validation or remove it from the interface.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.47  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: The reduction validators are too weak to protect this area’s key boundaries. There is no explicit `K=2` validator, and `validate_homogeneous()` only checks “one PM and equal PM scores”, not deterministic tie-breaking, `COL/PAR` counts, or reassignment behavior, so the active-`K` bug above would not be caught.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit `K=2` and reassignment validators, and strengthen homogeneous tests to assert full role-count invariants and tie-break behavior.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
